result.title: REA: From Correct LLM Judgments to Safe Decision Delivery
result.summary: Generative safety guards must classify requests correctly and return outputs that applications can parse. Reasoning guards can improve classification accuracy while producing outputs that applications cannot parse. When applications cannot extract a correct prediction, fallback handling can allow harmful requests or block safe ones. We introduce Resolve--Express--Act (REA), a framework that traces judgments through parsing and fallback to application actions. Experiments on classifiers and safety guards show that correct predictions can appear in incorrectly formatted outputs. Parsing the safety verdict preserves the reasoning guard's accuracy advantage, while stricter explanation requirements reject additional correct predictions. Accepting formatting variations recovers most rejected correct predictions. Held-out tests confirm that output requirements and generation limits affect whether correct predictions can be parsed. In our fail-open replay, matching the parser to the output and fixing formatting reduced the fraction of harmful requests allowed despite correct guard judgments from 95.5% to 0%. A fixed-output comparison shows that model-based extraction can preserve guard verdicts, but is not automatically reliable; deterministic normalization already repairs the observed native-format failures. Fallback replay shows that the same correct prediction can lead to different safety actions depending on the parser and fallback policy, including allowing requests the guard correctly identifies as harmful.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 REA 框架，把 LLM 安全守护模型的判断沿「解析—回退—应用动作」链路追踪，实验表明正确判断常出现在格式不合规的输出中，匹配解析器并规范格式可把误放行的有害请求比例大幅降低。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「判断正确」与「下游能否提取使用」分离评测的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态已含正确信息、但答案未使用或无法解码的类似现象，也可借鉴其解析匹配与前缀约束等做法。
